# Dataset explanation

10x Genomics obtained fresh frozen mouse kidney tissue (Strain C57BL/6)from BioIVT Asterand. The tissue was embedded and cryosectioned as described in Visium Spatial Protocols - Tissue Preparation Guide (Demonstrated Protocol CG000240). Tissue sections of 10 µm thickness were placed on Visium Gene Expression Slides.

The Visium kidney data to run this tutorial can be found [here](https://support.10xgenomics.com/spatial-gene-expression/datasets/1.0.0/V1_Mouse_Kidney)

Visium technology:

![](images/general_figs/visium_technology.png)

# Set up Giotto Environment

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Install Giotto Suite once (see the Installation page)
install.packages("GiottoUtils",
    repos = c("https://giotto-suite.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
GiottoUtils::suite_install(ref = "disk_full", install_arrow = TRUE)
```

# Giotto global instructions and preparations

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(Giotto)

# 1. set working directory
results_folder <- "/path/to/results/"
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
## create instructions
instructions <- createGiottoInstructions(save_dir = results_folder, 
                                         save_plot = TRUE, 
                                         show_plot = FALSE, 
                                         return_plot = FALSE)

## provide path to visium folder
data_path <- "/path/to/data/"
```

# Create Giotto object & process data

```{r, eval=FALSE}
## directly from visium folder
visium_kidney <- createGiottoVisiumObject(
    visium_dir = data_path,
    expr_data = "raw",
    png_name = "tissue_lowres_image.png",
    gene_column_index = 2,
    instructions = instructions
)

## check metadata
pDataDT(visium_kidney)

# check available image names
showGiottoImageNames(visium_kidney) # "image" is the default name

## show aligned image
spatPlot(gobject = visium_kidney, 
         cell_color = "in_tissue", 
         show_image = TRUE,
         point_alpha = 0.7)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="80%", fig.align="center"}
knitr::include_graphics("images/visium_mouse_kidney/0-spatPlot2D.png")
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
## subset on spots that were covered by tissue
metadata <- pDataDT(visium_kidney)
in_tissue_barcodes <- metadata[in_tissue == 1]$cell_ID

visium_kidney <- subsetGiotto(visium_kidney, 
                              cell_ids = in_tissue_barcodes)

## filter
visium_kidney <- filterGiotto(
    gobject = visium_kidney,
    expression_threshold = 1,
    feat_det_in_min_cells = 50,
    min_det_feats_per_cell = 1000,
    expression_values = "raw",
    verbose = TRUE
)

## normalize
visium_kidney <- normalizeGiotto(gobject = visium_kidney, 
                                 scalefactor = 6000, 
                                 verbose = TRUE)

## add gene & cell statistics
visium_kidney <- addStatistics(gobject = visium_kidney)

## visualize
spatPlot2D(gobject = visium_kidney, 
           show_image = TRUE, 
           point_alpha = 0.7)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="80%", fig.align="center"}
knitr::include_graphics("images/visium_mouse_kidney/1-spatPlot2D.png")
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
spatPlot2D(gobject = visium_kidney, 
           show_image = TRUE, 
           point_alpha = 0.7,
           cell_color = "nr_feats", 
           color_as_factor = FALSE)
```

# Clustering

```{r, eval=FALSE}
## sNN network (default)
visium_kidney <- createNearestNetwork(gobject = visium_kidney,
                                      dimensions_to_use = 1:10, 
                                      k = 15)

## Leiden clustering
visium_kidney <- doLeidenCluster(gobject = visium_kidney, 
                                 resolution = 0.4, 
                                 n_iterations = 1000)

plotUMAP(gobject = visium_kidney, 
         cell_color = "leiden_clus", 
         show_NN_network = TRUE, 
         point_size = 2.5)
```

# Cell type marker gene detection

## gini

```{r, eval=FALSE}
markers_gini <- findMarkers_one_vs_all(
    gobject = visium_kidney,
    method = "gini",
    expression_values = "normalized",
    cluster_column = "leiden_clus",
    min_featss = 20,
    min_expr_gini_score = 0.5,
    min_det_gini_score = 0.5
)

topgenes_gini <- markers_gini[, head(.SD, 2), by = "cluster"]$feats

# violinplot
violinPlot(visium_kidney,
           feats = unique(topgenes_gini), 
           cluster_column = "leiden_clus",
           strip_text = 8, 
           strip_position = "right")
```

# Cell-type annotation

Visium spatial transcriptomics does not provide single-cell resolution, making cell type annotation a harder problem. Giotto provides 3 ways to calculate enrichment of specific cell-type signature gene list:

-   PAGE
-   rank
-   hypergeometric test

# Spatial grid

```{r, eval=FALSE}
visium_kidney <- createSpatialGrid(
    gobject = visium_kidney,
    sdimx_stepsize = 400,
    sdimy_stepsize = 400,
    minimum_padding = 0
)

spatPlot(visium_kidney,
         cell_color = "leiden_clus", 
         show_grid = TRUE,
         grid_color = "red", 
         spatial_grid_name = "spatial_grid")
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="80%", fig.align="center"}
knitr::include_graphics("images/visium_mouse_kidney/18-spatPlot2D.png")
```

## Spatial co-expression patterns

Group spatial genes into co-expression modules: genes whose expression is correlated across neighbouring spots in the spatial network. See the [spatial co-expression modules](spatial_coexpression_modules.html) tutorial for details.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
my_spatial_genes <- km_spatialfeats[1:500]$feats

coexpr <- spatialCoexpression(visium_kidney,
                              feats = my_spatial_genes,
                              spatial_network_name = "Delaunay_network",
                              n_modules = 8,
                              return_gobject = FALSE)
coexpr$summary

# genes most correlated with one gene
top10_genes <- sort(coexpr$cor["Napsa", ], decreasing = TRUE)[2:11]
top10_genes

spatFeatPlot2D(visium_kidney,
               expression_values = "scaled",
               feats = c("Napsa", names(top10_genes)[1:3]), 
               point_size = 3)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="80%", fig.align="center"}
knitr::include_graphics("images/visium_mouse_kidney/23-spatFeatPlot2D.png")
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
heatmapCoexpression(visium_kidney, coexpr)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="60%", fig.align="center"}
knitr::include_graphics("images/visium_mouse_kidney/24-heatmapCoexpression.png")
```

Store the modules in the giotto object: each gene's module is added to the feature metadata and a score per module and spot as the spatial enrichment "spatial_module".

```{r, eval=FALSE}
visium_kidney <- spatialCoexpression(visium_kidney,
                                     feats = my_spatial_genes,
                                     spatial_network_name = "Delaunay_network",
                                     n_modules = 8)

showGiottoSpatEnrichments(visium_kidney)

spatCellPlot(visium_kidney,
             spat_enr_names = "spatial_module",
             cell_annotation_values = as.character(coexpr$summary$module),
             point_size = 1.5, 
             cow_n_col = 4)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="80%", fig.align="center"}
knitr::include_graphics("images/visium_mouse_kidney/26-spatCellPlot2D.png")
```

# HMRF domains

Find spatial domains with a hidden Markov random field (HMRF). HMRF works best on a few spatially informed values per spot, here the co-expression module scores from above. `runHMRF()` fits several `betas` (the strength of the spatial smoothing) in one call; `hmrfSummary()` compares them. See the [spatial domains](spatial_domains.html) tutorial for details.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# HMRF requires a fully connected network!
visium_kidney <- createSpatialNetwork(gobject = visium_kidney,
                                      minimum_k = 2,
                                      name = "Delaunay_full")

visium_kidney <- runHMRF(visium_kidney,
                         spat_enr_name = "spatial_module",
                         spatial_network_name = "Delaunay_full",
                         k = 5,
                         betas = c(0, 2, 5, 10))
hmrfSummary(visium_kidney)

## visualize
spatPlot(gobject = visium_kidney,
         cell_color = "hmrf_k5_b0",
         point_size = 5)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="80%", fig.align="center"}
knitr::include_graphics("images/visium_mouse_kidney/27-spatPlot2D.png")
```
